Product News
QUANTUM APPLICATIONS
MISSolve MIS problems for complex optimization challenges.
QEKQuantum-powered graph machine learning for advanced data analysis.
QUBOTackle Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization problems efficiently.
QUANTUM SDKS
QoolQitSimplified algorithm development for neutral atom quantum computers.
PulserDesign and simulate pulse sequences for quantum hardware and simulations.
Pulser StudioZero-code visual platform to program quantum computers without coding.
EXECUTION
QPU & EmulatorsExplore Pasqal QPUs and emulators available on the cloud or locally on your machine.
Pasqal CloudExecute quantum jobs on QPUs or emulators via our cloud platform.
Third-party Cloud ProvidersAccess Pasqal hardware through Google Cloud, Azure, OVHCloud, or Scaleway.

Error handling

Compilation errors with max_energy profile

Section titled “Compilation errors with max_energy profile”

At compilation several error might occur. In this notebook we describe the most common ones, show what are the typical error messages and how to interpret them and explain how to handle them.

Let us start by defining a simple quantum program:

We observe there that the compilation was successful and we can access the compiled sequence.

Let us now explore different cases where different error messages might. First let us define a small function that output the quantum program we want to compile:

Error 1: Amplitude too large

Section titled “Error 1: Amplitude too large”

In this case the compilation routine will try to rescale the register in such a way to maintain the same relative amplitudes of the drive. If the amplitude of the drive is too large, the register may become too large, leading to an overflow error.

After rescaling the input program to the maximum energy scale available for the selected device, the following exception was raised:

The register's maximum radial distance went over the maximum value allowed.
To compile this program on the selected device `AnalogDevice`, the maximum radial distance must be below 2.7547915763674697

What happened?

Section titled “What happened?”

We selected an amplitude that is 100 times larger than the maximum atomic pair-wise interaction. The compilation routine automatically attempted to employ the maximum allowed amplitude and rescale the register accordingly: that is in such a way to have the a value of interaction at nearest neighobr that matches the value of the amplitude. In doing so, the register size increased, leading to an overflow error.

Error 2: detuning too large

Section titled “Error 2: detuning too large”
After rescaling the input program to the maximum energy scale available for the selected device, the following exception was raised:

The drive's maximum absolute detuning went over the maximum value allowed.
To compile this program on the selected device `AnalogDevice`, set the maximum absolute detuning below 10.000000000000139

What happened?

Section titled “What happened?”

We selected a detuning that is 20 times larger than the maximum atomic pair-wise interaction. The compilation routine automatically rescales the amplitude to the maximum allowed value and all the other quantities accordingly. Hence, it rescaled the register and the detuning. This time the register is fitting the device but the detuning value goes beyond the allowed bounds.

Error 3: duration too long

Section titled “Error 3: duration too long”
After rescaling the input program to the maximum energy scale available for the selected device, the following exception was raised:

The drive's duration went over the maximum value allowed.
To compile this program on the selected device `AnalogDevice`, set the drive's duration below 7.5398223686154004

What happened?

Section titled “What happened?”

The compilation profile max_energy automatically rescales the amplitude to the maximum allowed value and all the other quantities accordingly. This means that also the time is rescaled. In particular, as explained in Adimensionalization and Compilation, when the amplitude is too large to fit the device and it has to be decreased and everything rescaled accordingly, then time is increased. In this case the total duration ended up being longer than the allowed value.
